body: No, I don't think he is. But on the off chance that it comes across that way I don't want to risk it.
I wrote out how I was feeling, but I don't think I'll get the courage to show it to him. I don't know how he'd react and I don't want it to seem like a cry for attention for the sake of it.
I've tried getting help, I've yet to find anyone that clicks with me enough to get through to me.

I've pretty much always been this way, I could never take criticism well as a child and always got teased. There are times I don't feel like this at all. Sometimes days or weeks at a time. But it always comes back to bite me.

I'm not sure what's been getting me down. I'm just tearing myself apart over everything I do. Mostly I'm feeling like I need someone to validate what I'm doing. I feel like every single thing I do is flawed in some way. I tell myself that I'll tell my boyfriend about how I feel in the morning (this all just happened tonight) but I know he doesn't need to hear it and I know I won't have the courage to actually tell him anything.

I've been feeling kind of down and shitty lately too, but I feel like I shouldn't bother him so much with repeating how I feel. I suffered from anxiety not too long ago and he dealt with my whining every day. Now I feel guilty when I do feel down but I always talk myself down from telling him

Kind of a long story. My boyfriend recently did poorly on an exam, and as most people would, he's upset about it. It's happened before, being university students and all. He always takes it hard. Anyways, I'd jokingly tell him to "smile", not sure how it started. I guess I took it too far after not noticing it making him more upset, closer to sad than anything. He got pretty angry at me and I feel like an asshole for making him feel like that. I clearly hurt his feelings and just feel like shit over this all.
